name: dbq
blurb: Chinese abbreviation of 对不起 (duì bu qǐ), "sorry", used in casual chat
title: DBQ Meaning: What Does DBQ Mean in Chinese Chat?
description: DBQ is short for 对不起 (duì bu qǐ), "sorry". In Chinese chat it is a casual apology, often used before a blunt opinion. Examples and tone.
answer: DBQ is the pinyin initialism of 对不起 (duì bu qǐ), "sorry". In Chinese online chat it is a casual, low-key apology, lighter than writing the full word. It became popular in fan communities and teenage chat, and China Youth Daily explained it in a 2018 report on young people's internet slang. It is also used before a blunt opinion, like "sorry, but…".

body: Like XSWL (笑死我了) and ZQSG (真情实感, "real feelings"), DBQ takes the first letter of each pinyin syllable. Fan communities used such initialisms a lot: they are fast and work as an in-group code that outsiders don't read at a glance.
In October 2018 China Youth Daily defined DBQ as the pinyin initials of 对不起 and quoted the line "你连 dbq 都不知道，xswl！" ("You don't even know dbq? LMAO!").

ul: dbq，刚刚在开会没看到消息 (sorry, I was in a meeting and missed your message)
dbq 我又迟到了，奶茶我请 (sorry I'm late again, bubble tea's on me)
dbq，但这部剧真的很难看下去 (sorry, but this show is really hard to sit through)
dbq 说句实话，这个配色不太行 (sorry, honestly, this color scheme doesn't work)
dbq dbq！ (sorry sorry!), after an accidental spoiler

body: The first two are real apologies; the middle two are "sorry, but" before a critique.

body: DBQ suits small slips between friends. For a real mistake, or an apology to a boss, client or older person, the abbreviation looks careless; write 对不起 in full and explain.
And "dbq, but…" may not feel like an apology to the person being criticised, so use it with some care.

faq.a: No. It is an apology, just a very casual one.

faq.q: How do I reply to DBQ?
faq.a: 没事 (no problem) or 没关系 (it's fine) work; friends often reply 原谅你了 (forgiven) or a sticker.
Simply "sorry". The "dbq, but…" use is like "sorry, but…" in English.
